mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth for two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations adjust downward.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 growth and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth prospects improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures signals a strengthening demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer confidence and economic activity rise.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of HOUST and RSAFS increases on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate coupled with an increase in nonfarm payrolls signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending power and business confidence improve.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases and PAYEMS increases in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of UNRATE decreases and PAYEMS increases on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index (CPI) for two consecutive months signals inflationary pressures, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate tighter monetary policy.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between CPIAUCSL increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real personal consumption expenditures coupled with a decrease in housing starts signals a weakening demand environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer confidence and economic activity decline.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both decrease in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of RSAFS and HOUST decreases on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
